chapter: Early bands and New Orleans musicians
title: No church music; lawn parties and their drinks and admission
summary: He never played in church; lawn parties were in backyards with drinks and a small entry charge.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: By the way, did you ever play any music in church or anything? In church? No.
What religion are you going to?
I'm Lutheran. I know there are, they sure are jazzin' up a lot of hymns now. Yeah. Yeah. Spirituals and stuff. Yeah. I just wondered if any of those tunes were picked up that way.
No, we didn't play any. Not, not, not years ago. Most of that he played was lawn parties.

blocks.s: Mrs. Joe Loyacano (wife of Joe Loyacano)
blocks.x: They used to call them lawn parties. You'd get out in somebody's backyard and dance on Napoleon. That's what you used to have to dance on.
Yeah, them was lawn parties. Did they sell drinks at lawn parties? Sure, did they sell drinks, for sure they sold drinks.

blocks.s: Mrs. Joe Loyacano (wife of Joe Loyacano)

blocks.x: So beer, whiskey, anything you wanted you could get.
Did they have a charge to get in or any kind?
Yeah, sure, a mission charge to get in and dance. Two bits of ticket.
